description: How one checker did on one task: a line of the results.jsonl of a run. It is the task and how it ended, which is one of the five ways that a reply can be, with what the runner adds, or one of two ways that are the runner's own. A key that does not apply is left out.

Task.description: The task: one of the two questions of a case, and what the corpus says the answer is.

case.description: The id of the case: the path of its file in the corpus without the extension.

direction.description: Which of the two questions of the case was asked: the key of the case that has its label.

expected.description: The label of the corpus for the task; null where it claims nothing.

answer.description: a accepts every instance that is valid under b.

seconds.description: What the checker took for the task, as its adapter measured it: parsing each schema once, and the check.

wall_seconds.description: What the runner waited for the reply.

answer.description: Some instance is valid under b and invalid under a.

seconds.description: What the checker took for the task, as its adapter measured it: parsing each schema once, and the check.

message.description: A text for a person: what the checker says about its no.

wall_seconds.description: What the runner waited for the reply.

witness.description: The counterexample that the checker gave, with what a validator made of it. The key is left out where the checker gave none.

Unknown.description: The checker ran and declined to answer.

answer.description: The checker ran and declined to answer.

seconds.description: What the checker took for the task, as its adapter measured it: parsing each schema once, and the check.

reason.description: What kind of reason the checker had, in a word or two that are the same for every task declined for it, such as the keyword that it does not support. `diff` counts the declined tasks by it.

message.description: A text for a person: the reason in full.

wall_seconds.description: What the runner waited for the reply.

Error.description: The checker failed, by an exception or by rejecting a schema.

failure.description: There is no answer, because the checker failed.

message.description: A text for a person: the error.

seconds.description: What the checker took for the task, as its adapter measured it: parsing each schema once, and the check.

wall_seconds.description: What the runner waited for the reply.

Timeout.description: The checker did not answer in time: it stopped itself, or the runner stopped waiting and killed it.

failure.description: There is no answer, because the time ran out.

wall_seconds.description: What the runner waited for the reply.

Unsupported.description: The checker was not asked, because the draft that it reads cannot express one of the schemas.

failure.description: There is no answer, because the checker was not asked.

message.description: A text for a person: what the draft cannot express.

Crash.description: The process of the adapter died, did not start, or gave a line that is no reply.

failure.description: There is no answer, because the adapter is at fault.

message.description: A text for a person: what happened.

wall_seconds.description: What the runner waited for the reply.

Witness.description: The counterexample that a checker gave with a no, and what a validator made of it. The validator reads the two schemas as the labels of the corpus do: as draft 2020-12, with format asserted.

Checked.description: The validator looked at the counterexample.

counterexample.description: An instance that is valid under b and invalid under a. The key is left out where there is none: null is an instance.

confirmation.description: confirmed: it is valid under b and invalid under a, as it has to be. not_an_instance: b rejects it, so a did not have to accept it. accepted: a accepts it, so it tells the two apart in nothing. With either of the last two the no counts as a wrong answer.

Unchecked.description: The validator did not look at the counterexample.

counterexample.description: An instance that is valid under b and invalid under a. The key is left out where there is none: null is an instance. It is left out too where it held a number that is none in JSON, and could not be kept.

confirmation.description: That it was not looked at.

message.description: A text for a person: why the validator did not look at it.
